title: Hazard Detection Unit
constraints: **Load-use hazard:** the instruction in EX is a load (`ex_mem_read`) whose `ex_rd` (≠ x0) matches a source register that the ID instruction actually uses.
**Taken branch** in EX: the instructions in IF and ID are on the wrong path.
`stall = load_use && !ex_branch_taken`: freeze PC and IF/ID. No point stalling a wrong-path instruction.
`id_ex_bubble = load_use || ex_branch_taken` (insert a NOP into ID/EX). `if_id_flush = ex_branch_taken`. Purely combinational.
hints: Write the load-use condition as one Boolean expression. Don't forget the `ex_rd != 0` term: nothing ever depends on x0.
Only compare a source register if the instruction uses it. An `addi` has no rs2, for example.
The branch outranks the stall: squashing the ID instruction resolves the load-use hazard too.

examples.title: load-use
examples.input: EX: lw x5; ID: add x6, x5, x7 (uses rs1 = x5)

examples.title: x0
examples.input: EX: lw x0 (rd = 0); ID uses x0
